{{Short description|British crown jeweller (1942–2026)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''David Vyvyan Thomas'''<ref name="telegraph">{{cite web | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/the_queens_diamond_jubilee/9305632/How-the-Queens-man-about-crowns-brought-sparkle-to-her-celebrations.html | title=How the Queen’s man about crowns brought sparkle to her celebrations | publisher=The Telegraph | date=June 2, 2012 | accessdate=September 1, 2013 | author=Middleton, Christopher}}</ref> {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MVO}} (21 July 1942 – 18 January 2026) was the [[Crown Jeweller]] for the [[British monarchy]]. He worked for the Royal Family from 1991 until his retirement in 2007 as an employee of [[Garrard & Co]]. He retained three royal warrants.{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}

==Life and career==
Thomas was the son of a [[Swansea]] chemist.<ref name="telegraph" /> At the age of 17, he joined his first employer Collingwood of Conduit Street as a postboy and jewellery-cleaner.<ref name="telegraph"/>

[[Charles III|Prince Charles]] "engineered" his move to Garrard & Co of Regent Street.<ref name="telegraph"/> Thomas originally worked for a competitor of Garrard's, but the rival company took an interest in Thomas and in 1986 they [[Executive search|headhunted]] him.<ref name="telegraph" /> Prince Charles enjoyed his work so much that he recommended him to the Queen, and he eventually was appointed to take over from former Crown Jeweller [[Bill Summers (jeweller)|Bill Summers]].<ref name="telegraph" />

Thomas designed the wedding rings for [[Diana Spencer]] and Prince Charles, and was Diana's personal jeweller until her death.<ref name="SmithsonianAssociates">{{Cite web|url=https://smithsonianassociates.org/ticketing/tickets/227243|title=A Day with David Thomas, Britain’s Former Royal Crown Jeweler - Smithsonian Associates|website=smithsonianassociates.org}}</ref> When Thomas retired at the age of 65 in July 2007, Garrard was replaced as the Royal Jeweller, after having the role since 1843. Thomas had held the Monarch's personal Royal warrant for the position since 1991. Contrary to reports, Garrard noted that Thomas was not retiring from the company until 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.standard.co.uk/news/garrard-to-lose-royal-jeweller-role-7084953.html|title=Garrard to lose Royal Jeweller role|date=February 10, 2007|website=Evening Standard}}</ref>

In 2017, Thomas worked for [[Cleave and Company]]. That year, he was commissioned through the company to make [[Meghan Markle]]'s engagement ring. It sourced a diamond from [[Botswana]] and several smaller diamonds that had belonged to [[Princess Diana]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/lifestyle/article/jeweller-wont-make-replicas-for-meghan-markles-ring/|title=Jeweller won't make replicas for Meghan Markle's ring|first=Hilary|last=Fox|date=December 6, 2017|website=CTVNews}}</ref>

Thomas died from complications of Alzheimer's disease on 18 January 2026, at the age of 83.<ref>{{cite news |title=David Thomas obituary: crown jeweller at heart of royal pomp |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/obituaries/article/david-thomas-obituary-crown-jeweller-at-heart-of-royal-pomp-zr539ds8n |access-date=20 January 2026 |publisher=The Times |date=20 January 2026}}</ref>

==Awards==
Thomas was appointed a [[Member of the Royal Victorian Order]] (MVO) in the [[2007 Birthday Honours]].<ref name="telegraph" /><ref>United Kingdom list: {{London Gazette |date=15 June 2007 |issue=58358 |pages=4 |supp=1}}</ref>
